definition_en: a person trained to treat sick people, or a university title
core_image: 诊室里一位穿白大褂的医生正在看病历
scene: 诊室里一位穿白大褂的医生正在看病历。The doctor checks his throat.
sceneCN: 这里 doctor 是「医生」（第 01 个义项）；句意是医生检查他的喉咙。

senses.title: A person trained to treat sick people
senses.definition: someone who has been trained to treat illness and injuries
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、给人治病的人
senses.example: The doctor checks his throat.
senses.why: Latin docere means to teach, and doctor first named a learned teacher; because learned men were consulted about illness, the title passed to those who treat the sick.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 docere 意为「教」，doctor 最初指有学问的教师；因为人们生病时常向有学问的人求教，这个称呼就转给了治病的人。

senses.title: The highest university title
senses.definition: the highest academic title given by a university
senses.definitionCN: 大学授予的最高学术头衔
senses.example: Her father is a doctor of law.
senses.why: The old sense of a learned teacher survived in the university: the top degree still makes its holder a doctor, teacher of the field.
senses.whyCN: 「有学问的教师」这个旧义在大学里保留下来：最高学位仍让获得者成为 doctor，即这一领域的授业者。

sceneCN: 这里 dollar 是「元」（第 01 个义项）；句意是这本书要十美元。

senses.title: The unit of money in the US and some other countries
senses.definition: the standard unit of money used in the United States and several other countries
senses.definitionCN: 美国等一些国家使用的货币单位
senses.example: The book costs ten dollars.
senses.why: The word comes from German Taler, the name of a large silver coin; that coin spread across trade routes and its name became the standard money unit in many countries.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自德语 Taler，是一种大银币的名字；这种银币沿贸易路线流通，名字就成了许多国家的货币单位。

senses.title: One coin or note of this value
senses.definition: a coin or banknote worth one dollar
senses.definitionCN: 面值一元的硬币或纸币
senses.example: She put a dollar in his hand.
senses.exampleCN: 她把一元钱塞到他手里。
senses.why: The unit and the object that carries it share one name: a dollar is both the amount and the piece of money in your palm.
senses.whyCN: 单位与承载它的实物同名：a dollar 既是那个数目，也是你手心那张钱。

definition_en: to make a picture with a pen or pencil, or to pull something
core_image: 一张白纸上，一支铅笔正画出一个圆形的太阳
scene: 一张白纸上，一支铅笔正画出一个圆形的太阳。She draws a sun on the paper.
sceneCN: 这里 draw 是「画」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她在纸上画了个太阳。

senses.title: To make a picture with a pen or pencil
senses.definition: to make a picture or line with a pen, pencil or similar tool
senses.definitionCN: 用笔之类的工具画出图形或线条
senses.example: She draws a sun on the paper.
senses.why: Old English dragan meant to drag or pull, and dragging a pen across paper left a line, so the pulling sense gave birth to drawing.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 dragan 意为「拖、拉」，把笔在纸上拖动就会留下线条，「拉」的意思由此生出「画」。

senses.title: To pull something along
senses.definition: to pull something behind or towards you
senses.definitionCN: 把东西往后或往自己这边拖
senses.example: The horse draws the cart up the hill.
senses.why: This is the oldest sense of the word: dragan named the physical act of pulling a load along the ground.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最老的意思：dragan 指把重物沿着地面拖动的动作。

senses.title: To attract people or attention
senses.definition: to make people come or look
senses.definitionCN: 把人引过来或让目光聚过来
senses.example: The singer drew a large crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 那位歌手引来一大群人。
senses.why: Pulling and attracting share one picture: something exerts a force and people move towards it, as if drawn by a rope.
senses.whyCN: 「拖」和「吸引」共用一个画面：有东西施加拉力，人就朝它移动，像被绳子牵过去。

senses.title: A result with no winner
senses.definition: an end to a game in which both sides have the same score
senses.definitionCN: 比赛结束时双方得分相同
senses.example: The match ended in a draw.
senses.why: When two sides are evenly matched, neither pulls the other over, so the game is said to end in a draw, as if the rope stayed still.
senses.whyCN: 双方势均力敌时谁也拉不动谁，比赛就成了 draw，好像绳子停在原地。

definition_en: a woman's garment, or to put clothes on
core_image: 一件蓝色连衣裙挂在衣柜前，裙摆轻轻摆动
scene: 一件蓝色连衣裙挂在衣柜前，裙摆轻轻摆动。She wears a blue dress to the party.
sceneCN: 这里 dress 是「连衣裙」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她穿一条蓝裙去参加聚会。

senses.title: A woman's one-piece garment
senses.definition: a piece of clothing for a woman or girl that covers the body and part of the legs
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖身体和部分腿部的一件式女装
senses.example: She wears a blue dress to the party.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿一条蓝裙去参加聚会。
senses.why: Old French dresser meant to arrange or prepare, and the noun came to name the arranged garment; English kept it for the one-piece woman's outfit.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 dresser 意为「整理、准备」，名词先指整理好的衣着，英语用它专指一件式的女装。

senses.title: To put clothes on someone
senses.definition: to put clothes on yourself or on another person
senses.definitionCN: 给自己或别人穿上衣服
senses.example: He dresses the baby after her bath.
senses.exampleCN: 他给洗完澡的宝宝穿衣服。
senses.why: The verb kept the old French sense of arranging: getting dressed is putting your clothes in order on your body.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了古法语「整理」的意思：穿衣就是把衣服一件件理到身上。

senses.title: Clothing of a particular style
senses.definition: clothes of a particular kind or for a particular occasion
senses.definitionCN: 某一类或某一场合穿的衣服
senses.example: The dancers wore national dress.
senses.why: Because the word once meant the whole arranged outfit, it still names a style of clothing, as in national dress or evening dress.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原本指整理好的一整套衣着，所以至今仍指某种风格的服装，如 national dress、evening dress。

senses.title: The number 18
senses.definition: the number between seventeen and nineteen
senses.definitionCN: 十七和十九之间的那个数
senses.example: She turns eighteen this year.
senses.why: Old English had eahtatīene, "eight-ten", a compound that literally counted eight beyond ten, and the modern form kept that build.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 eahtatīene 字面是「八加十」，把十之外的八个数合在一起，现代形式保留了这个构词。

senses.title: A group of eighteen things
senses.definition: eighteen people or things taken as a set
senses.definitionCN: 十八个人或十八样东西合为一组
senses.example: Eighteen of the seats were taken.
senses.why: Like other numbers, eighteen works as a noun when it counts a set, as in eighteen of the seats or eighteen students.
senses.whyCN: 和其他数词一样，十八用来数一组东西时作名词，如 eighteen of the seats、eighteen students。

senses.title: The age of eighteen years
senses.definition: the age of eighteen, often the age when a person becomes an adult
senses.definitionCN: 十八岁的年龄，常是成年的界限
senses.example: He left home at eighteen.
senses.why: Age is spoken of with the plain number, so at eighteen means at the age of eighteen, the point many countries mark as adulthood.
senses.whyCN: 说年龄时直接用数词，所以 at eighteen 就是十八岁那年，许多国家把这里当作成年的界线。

definition_en: a very large animal with a long trunk
core_image: 一头大象站在河边，用长鼻子吸起水来
scene: 一头大象站在河边，用长鼻子吸起水来。The elephant sprays water with its trunk.
sceneCN: 这里 elephant 是「大象」（第 01 个义项）；句意是大象用鼻子喷水。

senses.title: A very large animal with a long trunk
senses.definition: a huge animal with thick grey skin, large ears and a long trunk
senses.definitionCN: 皮厚、耳大、鼻子很长的巨型动物
senses.example: The elephant sprays water with its trunk.
senses.why: Greek elephas named ivory before it named the animal; the word reached English through Latin and first meant the tusks, then the creature that carried them.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 elephas 先指象牙，后指这种动物；这个词经拉丁语进入英语，最初指象牙，再指长着象牙的动物。

senses.title: Something large and costly to keep
senses.definition: a big thing that costs more to keep than it is worth, especially in the phrase white elephant
senses.definitionCN: 又大又费钱、留着不如丢掉的东西，常见于 white elephant 一语
senses.example: The old stadium became a white elephant.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧体育场成了个大包袱。
senses.why: An elephant is enormous and expensive to feed, so a costly object nobody can use was pictured as one, usually called white elephant.
senses.whyCN: 大象体形巨大、饲养昂贵，于是没人用得上的费钱之物被比作大象，常说成 white elephant。
